039252_7/98.html:
smx4 — can the Michel alone prove the stop? (doc pdvd/70, proposal P1)
Today's production found a Michel at the end of this muon (michel_found 1) but did not call the muon a stopper: is_stm 0, rejected by no_bragg (the dQ/dx at the end does not rise enough above the muon's plateau); shape_flat (the dQ/dx shape near the end fits a flat MIP profile better than a Bragg peak).
Please select — judge from the picture (3-D and wire views), not from the Michel's energy and length in the chain's-answer box:
1. The verdict (one button)
  • STM + MICHEL — the muon stops inside the detector and an electron starts at its end. Then set the Michel radio to attached, detached dots or both (the button is refused while it reads “not set”).
  • STM, no Michel — the muon stops, but you see no Michel.
  • THRU — the muon does not stop here: it goes on past the “Michel”, or leaves through a wall or a dead region. The chain's “Michel” is then a delta ray, a crossing track or a piece of the muon.
  • FRAG → … if this cluster is only part of the muon (give the whole muon's verdict); MESSY if it is not one track; UNCLEAR if you cannot tell.
2. If the muon stops but the chain's Michel is the wrong object (it took a delta ray or a gamma, and the real Michel is elsewhere or missed), write that in notes before clicking the verdict.
3. The pin: move it only if the muon's true end is not where the fit ends. A verdict click saves the row; after moving the pin or editing the notes, press SAVE this item. Then next unlabelled >>.

Today's production found a Michel at the end of this muon (michel_found 1) but did not call the muon a stopper: is_stm 0, rejected by shape_flat (the dQ/dx shape near the end fits a flat MIP profile better than a Bragg peak); continuation (a collinear MIP-like track leaves the stop); stop_near_boundary (the stop lies inside the fiducial margin of a detector boundary).
Please select — judge from the picture (3-D and wire views), not from the Michel's energy and length in the chain's-answer box:
1. The verdict (one button)
  • STM + MICHEL — the muon stops inside the detector and an electron starts at its end. Then set the Michel radio to attached, detached dots or both (the button is refused while it reads “not set”).
  • STM, no Michel — the muon stops, but you see no Michel.
  • THRU — the muon does not stop here: it goes on past the “Michel”, or leaves through a wall or a dead region. The chain's “Michel” is then a delta ray, a crossing track or a piece of the muon.
  • FRAG → … if this cluster is only part of the muon (give the whole muon's verdict); MESSY if it is not one track; UNCLEAR if you cannot tell.
2. If the muon stops but the chain's Michel is the wrong object (it took a delta ray or a gamma, and the real Michel is elsewhere or missed), write that in notes before clicking the verdict.
